newsitem.title: ALBANIA: French marines sweep Albanian port for guerrillas.
newsitem.headline: French marines sweep Albanian port for guerrillas.

text.p: French marines made a pre-dawn sweep of Durres harbour on Tuesday before the arrival of more than 1,000 troops following reports there might be a guerrilla attack, a French military official said.

A senior French military official said the 60 French marines inspected the western Albanian port between 3.30 a.m. and 4 a.m. (0130 and 0200 GMT) after Italian intelligence officers had warned of the possibility the landing force would be attacked.

"We got information last night from the Italians that there were rumours of terrorist actions in Durres," the senior French official said. "Because we didn't take any risks, we sent a sufficient number of commandos to secure the harbour."

A multinational force of more than 1,000 French, Spanish and Italian troops on a U.N.-backed mission to protect humanitarian aid convoys began landing at 7.00 a.m. (0500 GMT). The landing in Durres, 40 km (25 miles) west of Tirana, started one hour later than planned.
The French military official, who declined to be named, said French intelligence had not been able to confirm the reports. The marines inspected the water and entire port area, he said.
Another French officer, lieutenant colonel Gerard du Bois, said the troops were prepared for the mission. Asked if they were worried about an attack, he said:
"The risks are high where there are a lot of arms in circulation. We are not particularly frigthened. We have the capacity to defend ourselves."
Nearly 300 Albanians have been killed and more than 700 injured during weeks of armed insurrection that followed the collapse of dubious get-rich-quick investment schemes.
Tens of thousands of weapons ended up in the hands of mafias and ordinary Albanians after raids on abandoned state armouries.
Durres, 40 km (25 miles) west of Tirana, and the capital itself are two of the three entry points for the operation.
Greece, Turkey, Austria, Denmark and Romania are also contributing soldiers to the mission.
